text:
jane_cust: Hey team — hitting a bunch of mid-stream aborts from the streaming API. Client gets a few `data:` chunks then connection drops. Only happens on mobile (T‑Mobile) devices, ~10–30s into the stream. Any quick checks?

alex.k: thanks for the report — can you paste the raw client logs + the x-request-id from the failing call? Also which SDK / EventSource implementation are you using?

jane_cust: Using a React Native app, polyfilled EventSource. Example client log: "EVENT: data chunk, 512 bytes" then "SOCKET: close (code=0)". x-request-id=cb2f9a71. Happens for ~30% of mobile sessions.

julian_p: @alex.k @maya_rice tagging in case this is NAT mapping or carrier aggressive idle-timeout. Mobile carriers will drop idle TCP mappings after short periods — if the client doesn't send keepalive, the server write fails mid-stream (broken pipe / EPIPE).

maya_rice: quick triage steps: 1) confirm server logs for x-request-id cb2f9a71 (we want to see if server returned a 2xx then saw write error) 2) ask customer to enable client-side SSE comment pings `: ping

` every 15s 3) check any proxy/nginx timeouts in front of the runtime (keepalive_timeout, proxy_read_timeout).

alex.k: pulled logs for cb2f9a71 — server accepted the request, started streaming, final log entry is `write failed: broken pipe` after ~28s. nginx in front has proxy_read_timeout 60s, so not nginx. Suggests client or carrier dropped the mapping.

jane_cust: ok — how would I simulate this locally to repro for engineering?

julian_p: two simple repros: (a) on linux, use `tc qdisc add dev lo root netem loss 10% delay 100ms` to emulate flaky mobile and run your EventSource; (b) simulate abrupt socket kill with `socat - TCP:localhost:443,shut-down` or `pkill -f node` on the client to force FIN/RST mid-stream. Also try Chrome mobile emulation and toggle network.

maya_rice: also try adding an SSE comment keepalive:
```
const es = new EventSource(url);
// server-side or client can send comment lines like `: keepalive` every 15s
// e.g. server: `: keepalive

`
```
This will keep NAT mappings alive on many carriers.

support-bot: Billing note: partial streamed responses will still count tokens produced up to the point of termination. If you need a refund for repeated aborted sessions, open a billing ticket with sample x-request-ids.

alex.k: follow-ups for us: - add a small server-side ping comment every 20s as fallback for clients without keepalive - add more structured logging around `write failed` to capture peer addr and tcp resets - ops: can we surface a metric for `stream write failures` broken down by region/carrier? @sre-bot

sre-bot: filed infra ticket INF-892: add write-failure counts + last-peer-info to trace logs. Will also add a short-lived experiment to emit server comment pings for mobile-region routings.

jane_cust: perfect — I added client-side comment pings and saw the failures drop to ~3% in a small test. Thanks all, will keep you posted if anything resurfaces. :tada:

alex.k: great — leaving this thread open for a day to collect further x-request-ids if it reappears. If you hit a refund case, DM me the ids and we'll escalate billing. :thumbsup:
